title: October 30 — observed spatial atlas and transformer state that changes inference
summary: Two distinct new repositories. SweepAtlas is a practical webcam/MP4 feature-matching mosaic with keyframes, tile-backed 2-D observation storage, timeline scrubbing, and non-destructive contrast/sharpness export; not SLAM or a learned world model. TransformerX freezes pretrained DistilGPT-2 and trains recurrent state, adapters and router on synthetic silent-rule feedback. In a three-seed, nine-run sweep all routers use retained history (about 92.2% vs 80.46% marginal), and severing state access removes the gain. The multiplicative interaction router has no established advantage over simpler concat; dictionary and visual tasks remain near chance.

nodes.claim: Frozen pretrained DistilGPT-2 is adapted by trainable low-rank residual operators, per-stream 64-coordinate recurrent state and a reader/router that changes inference using earlier noisy feedback on a synthetic silent-rule task.
nodes.survived: Three-seed, nine-run GPU sweep: interaction/additive/concat mean test accuracy 92.27%/92.22%/92.23% versus 80.46% matched no-history marginal. State-read disconnection reduces means to 80.17%/80.65%/80.17%; restoring unchanged state recovers identical predictions. Source audit reports 6,144 trials per router per seed and validation-selected checkpoints.
nodes.killed: Interaction beats concat by only 0.038 percentage points on average; concat has lower test NLL in each seed and 4.02% fewer trainable parameters. No-feedback mean is 73.23%/71.25%/72.29% (unseen feedback marker is a distribution shift). Frozen dictionary language 23.96% and occluded-motion vision 24.74% remain at about four-way chance; no chat, continual-learning, router-specific causal benefit or GRU/window/token baseline victory follows.
nodes.era: October 30: spatial observations and state-conditioned transformer inference

nodes.claim: Local OpenCV webcam and uploaded-video mosaic builder: ORB/RANSAC view alignment, affine/homography transforms, keyframe re-anchoring, lazily allocated 2-D pixel tiles, transparent PNG export, and an interactive scrubbable video timeline.
nodes.survived: Executable webcam and MP4 pipeline, timeline scrub/step/play, 512-pixel default tiles, unobserved-area transparency, source-pixel-only blending, and non-destructive sharpness/contrast preview and export. Windows CI reports passing syntax, video/seek, filter/export, and synthetic planar alignment tests.
nodes.killed: Seeking previews frames but does not backfill skipped views. Older-keyframe re-anchoring is not global bundle adjustment or true 3-D SLAM; parallax, nonplanar rooms, independently moving objects and poor overlap can distort or break the mosaic. No learned geometry, object identity, or inference from unseen pixels; image enhancements do not restore missing information.

edges.why: TransformerX explicitly credits LoopAImemory as inspiration; both investigate history-dependent readouts, but TransformerX modifies a frozen pretrained transformer during its forward computation rather than only learning a final ridge readout.
TransformerX explicitly names RoundAndRound as inspiration for persistent-state experiments, but implements a different supervised recurrent adapter and has no slow residual-reawakening mechanism.

Both are independently implemented local-video instruments with timelines: Loopcraft trims and exports GIFs, whereas SweepAtlas aligns observations into a spatial mosaic. This is functional convergence, not a code fork.

motifs.title: Retained history changes the current computational path
motifs.description: LoopAImemory exposes temporal information to a trained readout; TransformerX causally disconnects an inference-time state access path and loses 9.81–12.96 pp. The nine-run results do not uniquely credit multiplicative routing or establish superiority over conventional recurrent/history baselines.

motifs.title: Spatial observation, uncertainty and imagination must be distinguished
motifs.description: SweepAtlas aligns measured pixels into an addressable 2-D image atlas. WorldModel explicitly separates observed evidence from imagined scene geometry; SihtiImageModel5 tests remembered pixels vs completion. Combining them is a future experiment, not completed 3-D reconstruction.

motifs.title: Inspectable video is useful without claiming learned world understanding
motifs.description: Loopcraft organizes time for clip/GIF export; SweepAtlas projects overlapping time samples into a spatial mosaic, retaining original imagery independently of display filters. Neither alone establishes depth, object permanence or scene understanding.
